title: Affine derived Hom of finite modules has quasi-coherent cohomology
statement: Let $A$ be a Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $U = \operatorname{Spec}(A)$, and let $M,N$ be finite $A$-modules [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], with associated $\mathcal O_U$-modules $\widetilde M,\widetilde N$ [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections]. Let $R\mathcal Hom_U$ be the derived internal Hom on $D(\mathcal O_U)$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] and $\mathcal H^q$ its cohomology sheaves [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. Then $\mathcal H^q(R\mathcal Hom_U(\widetilde M[0],\widetilde N[0]))=0$ for $q<0$, and for every integer $q\ge0$ it is quasi-coherent [pqf-def-coherent] and canonically isomorphic to $\widetilde{\operatorname{Ext}^q_A(M,N)}$, the associated sheaf of the Ext group [def-pc-ext] in the category of $A$-modules.

source.place: Tags 08DL, 00LP, 0A64, and 06XR: restriction of RHom, finite-free resolutions, cohomology of RHom, and computation of Ext from projective resolutions, specialized to an affine scheme

proof.text: Choose an exact finite-free resolution $\cdots\to F_1\to F_0\to M\to0$ by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-free-resolution-noetherian] (Tag 00LP), and put $E^{-i}=\widetilde{F_i}$ for $i\ge0$, with all positive terms zero. On each principal open $D(f)$, [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections] identifies the augmented complex with the localization of the module resolution at $f$. This remains exact by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact]. At a point $\mathfrak p$, [lem-weil-pbc-spec-tilde-stalk-localization] identifies the stalk complex with the localization at $A\setminus\mathfrak p$, which is exact by the same localization statement; hence [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-exact](5) gives a quasi-isomorphism $E^\bullet\to\widetilde M[0]$. Every $E^{-i}$ is finite free over $\mathcal O_U$ because $F_i$ is finite free over $A$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 00LP (lemma-resolution-by-finite-free), part (2); Perfect Complexes Tag 0A6H (lemma-quasi-coherence-internal-hom), proof of part (3)

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-derived-hom-finite-free-model] to $E^\bullet\to\widetilde M[0]$ and $\widetilde N[0]$. Thus $R\mathcal Hom_U(\widetilde M[0],\widetilde N[0])$ is represented by $\mathcal Hom^\bullet_U(E^\bullet,\widetilde N[0])$. For each $i\ge0$, $F_i\cong A^{n_i}$, so both $\mathcal Hom_U(\widetilde{F_i},\widetilde N)$ and $\widetilde{\operatorname{Hom}_A(F_i,N)}$ are canonically $\widetilde N^{n_i}$; the identifications commute with the differential induced by each $F_i\to F_{i-1}$. Hence the representing sheaf complex is termwise the associated-sheaf complex of $\operatorname{Hom}_A^\bullet(F^\bullet,N[0])$, with degree $q$ term $\widetilde{\operatorname{Hom}_A(F_q,N)}$ for $q\ge0$ and zero for $q<0$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0A6H (lemma-quasi-coherence-internal-hom), proof of part (3), citing Cohomology lemma-Rhom-complex-of-direct-summands-finite-free

proof.text: Associated sheaves commute with the cohomology of this complex: at a prime $\mathfrak p$, [lem-weil-pbc-spec-tilde-stalk-localization] identifies the stalk of every term and differential with localization at $\mathfrak p$; [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact] identifies the localized kernel, image and quotient with the corresponding cohomology of the localized complex; and [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-exact](5) detects the resulting isomorphism of sheaves. Consequently $\mathcal H^q(R\mathcal Hom_U(\widetilde M[0],\widetilde N[0]))\cong\widetilde{H^q(\operatorname{Hom}_A^\bullet(F^\bullet,N[0]))}$ for every integer $q$. In negative degrees the complex of Step 2 is zero, so these sheaves vanish.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0A6H (lemma-quasi-coherence-internal-hom), part (3), and its proof

proof.text: By [lem-sc-derived-hom-projective-resolution], the module Hom complex of Steps 2-3 represents $R\operatorname{Hom}_A(M[0],N[0])$; by [lem-sc-rhom-cohomology-ext-ring] (Tag 0A64), its degree-$q$ cohomology is canonically $\operatorname{Ext}^q_A(M,N)$ for $q\ge0$. Substitute this into Step 3. The isomorphism is canonical because both cited derived-Hom comparisons and the finite-free identifications of Step 2 commute with maps of resolutions. Finally [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections] says that the associated sheaf of each Ext module is quasi-coherent, giving the claimed quasi-coherence.
